A man drives at constant speed $v$ over a humpback bridge of circular shape and radius $r$. A set of scales in his seat shows his weight. He noticed the reading decreased as he passed over the top, and claimed that if he travelled fast enough the scales would read zero. Assess his statement.
questions.answer:
- At the top, the net force on the man points down to the centre of the circle: $mg-N=\dfrac{mv^2}{r}$.
- The scales read the normal force, $N=mg-\dfrac{mv^2}{r}$, which is less than $mg$ and decreases as $v$ increases.
- $N=0$ when $v=\sqrt{gr}$: gravity alone then provides exactly the centripetal force and he feels weightless.
- Above this speed the car and man leave the road as projectiles, and the scales still read zero.

His statement is therefore correct.

questions.question: A car of mass 1100 kg travels in a horizontal circle of radius 40 m on a track banked at $12^\circ$, at 5 m s⁻¹. Determine the period of the car around the track.
questions.answer: $$T=\frac{2\pi r}{v}=\frac{80\pi}{5}=50.3\text{ s}$$

questions.question: A car of mass 1100 kg travels in a horizontal circle of radius 40 m on a track banked at $12^\circ$, at 5 m s⁻¹. Determine the angular velocity of the car.
questions.answer: $$\omega=\frac vr=\frac{5}{40}=0.125\text{ rad s}^{-1}$$

questions.question: A car of mass 1100 kg travels in a horizontal circle of radius 40 m on a track banked at $12^\circ$, at 5 m s⁻¹. The car increases its speed until it can follow the path without any friction. Determine this speed.
questions.answer:
Vertically $N\cos\theta=mg$; horizontally $N\sin\theta=\dfrac{mv^2}{r}$. So $\tan\theta=\dfrac{v^2}{rg}$.
$$v=\sqrt{40\times9.8\tan12^\circ}=9.1\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

questions.question: The graph shows the acceleration due to gravity $g$ near Pluto against $\dfrac1{r^2}$, where $r$ is the distance from Pluto's centre. Determine $g$ at $3.0\times10^6$ m from the centre of Pluto.
questions.answer:
$\dfrac1{r^2}=1.11\times10^{-13}$ m⁻². The gradient is $\dfrac{0.617}{7.06\times10^{-13}}$, so
$$g\approx0.097\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

questions.question: The graph shows the acceleration due to gravity $g$ near Pluto against $\dfrac1{r^2}$, where $r$ is the distance from Pluto's centre. Use the graph to calculate the mass of Pluto.
questions.answer:
$g=\dfrac{GM}{r^2}$, so the gradient equals $GM$.
$$M=\frac{0.617}{7.06\times10^{-13}\times6.67\times10^{-11}}=1.31\times10^{22}\text{ kg}$$

questions.question: Two parallel wires carry currents $I_1=3.0$ A (wire X) and $I_2=5.0$ A (wire Y) in the same direction, 0.17 m apart over a length of 4.6 m. Determine the magnitude and direction of the force on wire Y caused by wire X.
questions.answer:
$$F=\frac{\mu_0I_1I_2\,l}{2\pi r}=\frac{2\times10^{-7}\times3.0\times5.0\times4.6}{0.17}=8.1\times10^{-5}\text{ N}$$
Parallel currents attract, so the force is to the left (towards X).

questions.question: Two coils are placed near each other. The left coil is connected to a battery and switch S; the right coil is connected to resistor $R$. Identify and explain the direction (left, right or zero) of the current in the resistor just after S is closed.
questions.answer: **Right.** Closing S creates a growing field, making the right end of the left coil a north pole. The changing flux through the right coil induces a current whose field opposes the change (Lenz's law), so its left end becomes a north pole. This requires current to the right through $R$.

questions.question: Two coils are placed near each other. The left coil is connected to a battery and switch S; the right coil is connected to resistor $R$. Identify and explain the direction (left, right or zero) of the current in the resistor after S has been closed for several seconds.
questions.answer: **Zero.** The current in the left coil is steady, so the flux through the right coil is not changing and no EMF is induced.

questions.question: An insulated wire forms a figure eight: a top circle of radius $r$ and a bottom circle of radius $2r$. A uniform magnetic field into the page is increasing at a constant rate. The EMF induced in the top circle is 1 V. Determine the magnitude of the total EMF induced in the whole loop.
questions.answer:
EMF is proportional to area, so the bottom circle has $4$ V. The crossover makes the two EMFs oppose:
$$\varepsilon=4-1=3\text{ V}$$

questions.question: An insulated wire forms a figure eight: a top circle of radius $r$ and a bottom circle of radius $2r$. A uniform magnetic field into the page is increasing at a constant rate. The EMF induced in the top circle is 1 V. Determine the direction of the force on the induced current at point A (bottom of the lower circle) due to the external field.
questions.answer: The larger circle's EMF dominates, giving an anticlockwise current in it. At A the current is to the right, so the force is **up the page** (opposing the increase in flux).

questions.question: A laser passes through two narrow slits $2.0\times10^{-4}$ m apart, producing the interference pattern shown on a screen. Determine the wavelength of the light.
questions.answer:
The first maximum is at $\theta=0.20^\circ$.
$$\lambda=d\sin\theta=2.0\times10^{-4}\sin0.20^\circ=7.0\times10^{-7}\text{ m}$$

questions.question: A laser passes through two narrow slits $2.0\times10^{-4}$ m apart, producing the interference pattern shown on a screen. Describe (and sketch) the effect of repeating the experiment with the slits further apart.
questions.answer: Since $\sin\theta=\dfrac{m\lambda}{d}$, a larger $d$ gives smaller angles: the maxima are closer together. The pattern is otherwise essentially the same.

questions.question:
Polarised light of intensity $I_0$ passes through a rotating polarising filter to a detector. The angle is zero where transmission is maximum.

| Angle (°) | 15 | 30 | 45 | 60 | 75 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Intensity (kW m⁻²) | 11.19 | 8.99 | 5.97 | 2.97 | 0.78 |

By plotting a suitable graph, assess whether the data support Malus's law.
questions.answer:
Malus's law is $I=I_0\cos^2\theta$, so plot $I$ against $\cos^2\theta$.

| $\cos^2\theta$ | 0.933 | 0.750 | 0.500 | 0.250 | 0.067 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $I$ (kW m⁻²) | 11.19 | 8.99 | 5.97 | 2.97 | 0.78 |

The points lie on a straight line through the origin (gradient about 12.0), so $I\propto\cos^2\theta$. The data support Malus's law.

questions.answer: $I_0$ is the value of $I$ at $\cos^2\theta=1$, the gradient of the $I$ against $\cos^2\theta$ graph: about $12.0$ kW m⁻².

questions.question: In 1865 James Clerk Maxwell published *A Dynamical Theory of the Electromagnetic Field*. Outline his contribution to our understanding of light.
questions.answer:
- His equations unified electricity and magnetism and predicted electromagnetic waves.
- Such waves are produced by oscillating (accelerating) charges.
- They consist of oscillating electric and magnetic fields, perpendicular to each other and to the direction of travel, which are self-propagating and need no matter.
- Their predicted speed, $c=\dfrac1{\sqrt{\mu_0\varepsilon_0}}=3.0\times10^8$ m s⁻¹, matched the measured speed of light. Maxwell concluded that light is an electromagnetic wave, one part of a spectrum of different frequencies.

questions.question: To measure the speed of light, a source emits a pulse that reaches a detector by path A (directly, 0.15 m) and by path B (via a mirror 6.00 m beyond the detector). The detector records the arrival times shown. Estimate the speed of light from this data.
“The Physics that explains the operation of the induction motor is the same Physics that explains back emf in DC motors.” With reference to the operation of both motors, justify this statement.
questions.answer:
**Common physics:** Faraday's law (a changing flux through a conductor induces an EMF) and Lenz's law (the induced effect opposes the change causing it).

**DC motor:** current in the coil in an external field experiences a force, giving a torque; the split ring commutator keeps the torque in one direction. As the coil rotates, the flux through it changes, inducing an EMF. By Lenz's law it opposes the supply: this is the back EMF, which reduces the current as speed rises.

**Induction motor:** AC in the stator windings produces a rotating magnetic field. This changes the flux through the conducting rotor, inducing an EMF and eddy currents (Faraday). These currents experience a force in the field which, by Lenz's law, acts to reduce the relative motion, so the rotor turns in the same direction as the rotating field.

Both rely on electromagnetic induction from relative motion between conductors and magnetic fields, governed by the same two laws, so the statement is justified.

questions.question: A spacecraft travels at $0.87c$ between Earth and Teegarden's Star, 12.51 light-years apart in Earth's frame. Calculate the distance of the journey in the spacecraft's frame.

A muon at rest decays in 2.2 µs, but when observed moving at relativistic speed its decay time is 8.8 µs. Explain how this provides evidence for special relativity and calculate the speed of the muons.
questions.answer:
Einstein's postulates predict that a moving clock is observed to run slow (time dilation). The longer decay time of the moving muons, measured by an observer relative to whom they move, is exactly this effect, which Newtonian physics cannot explain.
$$8.8=\frac{2.2}{\sqrt{1-v^2/c^2}}\Rightarrow\sqrt{1-v^2/c^2}=0.25$$
$$v=c\sqrt{1-0.0625}=0.968c=2.9\times10^8\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

questions.question: A negatively charged electroscope with a zinc plate on top has its gold leaf deflected outwards. When red light shines on the zinc, the leaf does not move. When ultraviolet light shines on it, the leaf falls immediately. Explain these observations.
questions.answer:
- Light consists of photons of energy $E=hf$; one photon gives all its energy to one electron.
- An electron is emitted only if $hf>\phi$, the work function of zinc ($K_{max}=hf-\phi$).
- Red photons have low frequency, with $hf<\phi$, so no electrons are emitted however intense the light. The charge, and the leaf, stay unchanged.
- UV photons have $hf>\phi$, so photoelectrons are ejected at once, with no build-up time.
- Removing electrons reduces the excess negative charge, so the repulsion between leaf and plate decreases and the leaf falls.

questions.question: The HR diagram shows regions A₁ (upper main sequence), A₂ (lower main sequence), B (giants), C (supergiants) and D (white dwarfs). Identify the region where p–p chain hydrogen fusion predominantly occurs in the core.
questions.answer: Region A₂ (main sequence stars below about 1.3 solar masses).

questions.question: The HR diagram shows regions A₁ (upper main sequence), A₂ (lower main sequence), B (giants), C (supergiants) and D (white dwarfs). Identify the region where CNO cycle hydrogen fusion predominantly occurs in the core.
questions.answer: Region A₁ (main sequence stars above about 1.3 solar masses).

questions.question: The HR diagram shows regions A₁ (upper main sequence), A₂ (lower main sequence), B (giants), C (supergiants) and D (white dwarfs). For a star starting in region A₂, describe its movement in the HR diagram as it ages, linking this to the changes occurring inside it.
questions.answer:
- **A₂ (main sequence):** hydrogen fuses to helium in the core for most of the star's life.
- **A₂ → B (red giant):** core hydrogen runs out, the core contracts and heats, and hydrogen fuses in a shell. The outer layers expand and cool, so luminosity rises and surface temperature falls (up and right). Helium then fuses to carbon in the core.
- **B → D (white dwarf):** helium fuel runs out and the outer layers are ejected as a planetary nebula. The exposed core is small and hot with no fusion, so it moves to low luminosity and high temperature (down and left), then slowly cools.

questions.question: Explain how the properties of stars can be determined from their spectra.
questions.answer:
- **Surface temperature:** a star radiates approximately as a black body. The peak wavelength of its continuous spectrum gives $T$ from Wien's law, $\lambda_{max}=b/T$.
- **Chemical composition:** cooler atmospheric gases absorb discrete wavelengths matching their electron transitions. Matching the absorption lines to laboratory patterns identifies the elements present.
- **Radial velocity:** the Doppler effect shifts all lines to longer wavelengths for a receding star (red shift) and shorter for an approaching one (blue shift). The size of the shift gives the speed.
- **Rotational velocity:** one limb approaches while the other recedes, so each line is broadened; the width indicates the rate of rotation.
- **Density (and luminosity class):** higher atmospheric pressure means more collisions and broader lines. Narrow lines indicate a low-density giant, broad lines a dense dwarf.
- Spectral class and luminosity class place the star on the HR diagram, from which luminosity and approximate radius and mass can be estimated.
